title: Angkor Wat
blurb: The largest religious monument in the world: Suryavarman II’s early-12th-century temple-mountain to Vishnu, 162.6 hectares ringed by a moat, with three raised galleries and a quincunx of five lotus-bud towers, the central spire rising 65 m.

sourceUrls.label: Archaeology Magazine: Tomb Raider review (2001 Angkor filming)
Criterion: In the Mood for Love (final scene at Angkor Wat)

systems.name: Moat and causeways
systems.description: The schematic moat ring (the real moat is 190 m wide with a 5 km perimeter), the west causeway with naga balustrades and guardian lions, and the east causeway.

systems.name: Outer enclosure
systems.description: The outer wall (3.6 km in reality), corner pavilions, and the west and east gopura entrance towers.

systems.name: First gallery
systems.description: The lowest of the three raised rectangular galleries, with its colonnade walls, corner towers and entrance porches.

systems.name: Second gallery
systems.description: The middle raised gallery with its walls, corner towers and the two libraries.

systems.name: Upper terrace and pyramid
systems.description: The uppermost terrace with the three-tiered pyramid, corner shrines and axial walkway.

systems.name: Central quincunx
systems.description: The five lotus-bud towers in quincunx: the 65 m central spire and its four satellites, the five peaks of Mount Meru.

systems.name: Bas-reliefs
systems.description: The extensive bas-relief panels lining the gallery walls, including the Churning of the Ocean of Milk.

systems.name: Stairways
systems.description: The grand stairs between levels and the famously steep stair to the central tower.

systems.name: Devatas
systems.description: Celestial dancer figures adorning the temple walls.
